sections.h2: Why Florida exteriors fail, and where we start
body: Paint on a Florida house rarely fails evenly. Afternoon sun bakes the south and west faces until they turn powdery and pale, while the north side can look nearly new. Lower courses of siding soak up splash-back and irrigation overspray and rarely dry out. Stucco expands in the midday heat, shrinks overnight, and opens fine cracks along the way. Doing exterior house painting in North Central Florida well means diagnosing each of those patterns elevation by elevation and pricing only the repairs every wall truly calls for.

During the site visit, your crew lead circles the house with a camera and tape, and checks any doubtful trim or stucco with a moisture meter. What you get back is an itemized scope of repairs, products, and coat counts, not a generic per-square-foot figure. Curious why some walls give out first? Our piece on exterior paint lifespan in Florida digs into it.

sections.h2: Prep: washing, repairs, and sealing the envelope
body: Peeling and blistering usually begin beneath the coating, not on top of it. So cleaning and repairs come before a single drop of paint. Each material gets a wash pressure suited to it, and the pressure and soft washing page explains how we kill mildew and algae without driving water behind lap siding.
bullets: Clean off algae and mildew, then let the walls dry completely
Scrape loose paint and sand edges so new coats lie flat
Cut out and replace rotten fascia, trim, and siding boards instead of hiding them
Re-caulk gaps at windows, doors, and trim joints, and reset nail pops
Prime every patched spot and any exposed wood
Mask windows, fixtures, hardware, plantings, and walkways

sections.h2: Coating systems for stucco, siding, and trim
body: Each substrate gets its own system. Clapboard, board-and-batten, and Hardie-style boards along with their trim receive 100% acrylic, which stays supple through summer heat and holds color under UV. Masonry and stucco that show hairline movement receive an elastomeric coating, a thick film that bridges small cracks so they do not reappear in the finish. Entry doors, porch railings, and shutters are coated in waterborne urethane enamel. Where stucco is broken rather than just crazed, it is fixed beforehand under our stucco repair service.

The specific Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore product for each surface is printed on your quote. Expect at least two complete coats, and where we spray, a second painter follows with a roller or brush to work the paint into stucco texture and wood grain. Trim, shutters, and doors can also be refreshed on their own through trim and molding painting.

sections.h2: Surfaces we paint and what each one needs
body: Every exterior material behaves differently in our climate, so the prep and product change from house to house. Painted stucco is the most common surface we see in newer neighborhoods; it holds moisture after rain and grows algae on shaded walls, so cleaning and crack treatment come first. Wood lap and board-and-batten siding, which turns up on many older Gainesville and High Springs houses, has to be scraped back to sound paint with every bare patch primed. Fiber-cement siding holds paint well but needs every butt joint and trim seam caulked. Painted block and brick need a breathable masonry-appropriate system and attention to efflorescence.

Trim, fascia, soffits, garage doors, front doors, and shutters are part of nearly every exterior. Visitors notice these details first, so they are sanded smooth, caulked tight at every joint, and finished in a tougher enamel wherever fingers and rain land. Weighing a new palette? Browse our notes on Gainesville's historic color schemes for ideas.

sections.h2: Weather, timing, and how long it takes
body: From October to May the air is drier and the daily thunderstorm is rarer, which is why we steer exterior jobs into those months. Summer projects still happen: the crew begins at daybreak, keeps the dew point in check so the film cures properly, and packs up the moment a cell shows on radar. Pushing on through a July afternoon to hit a deadline is exactly how fresh coatings rinse away or bubble. More on this in our guide to Florida weather and exterior paint.

Plan on three to seven working days for the whole outside of a house, with wash and dry days on top. After you approve the quote, a start date one to three weeks out is normal. Nobody has to stay home during outside work, but we do ask that sprinklers be turned off for the wash and paint days, and that cars be moved away from the driveway side of the house.

Our labor on the outside of your home is guaranteed in writing for up to 10 years, separate from whatever product warranty the paint maker provides. Nothing closes until you have walked the house with us and signed off, every flagged spot gets corrected beforehand, and we leave marked cans for future touch-ups. We paint homes from Lake City to Belleview; see our Gainesville exterior painting and Ocala exterior painting pages for local notes.

faqs.q: How long does exterior paint last in Florida?
faqs.a: That varies with sun exposure, preparation, and the coating used, and walls facing the afternoon sun always go first. A properly cleaned and repaired house finished in quality acrylic or elastomeric outlasts a rushed single coat by a wide margin, which is why we can back our outside work with a written warranty reaching 10 years.

faqs.q: When is the best time to paint a house exterior in Florida?
faqs.a: Aim for the cooler, drier months between October and May. We can still paint in summer by starting at sunrise, tracking dew point, and wrapping up before the afternoon thunderheads arrive.

faqs.q: Should stucco get elastomeric or acrylic paint?
faqs.a: Stucco with hairline cracks usually does best with an elastomeric coating, which flexes over movement. Sound, uncracked stucco can take a quality 100% acrylic. The call is made after we look at your walls, and the chosen product appears by name on your quote.

faqs.q: Do you fix rotted wood before painting?
faqs.a: Yes. Rotten fascia, trim, or siding is swapped for new material during prep, with each piece itemized up front. Paint over decay just buys a few months before it shows again.
